messages.subject: failed stack_alloc tests?
parts:
Everything definitely passes on my machine.

Could we still be running 32-bit mode on Windows? Or
is Windows int sizes (different than *nix) messing
things up? I created the test boundaries empirically
on my machine in clang++ knowing the test fixed things and just
looking for where the old behavior differs from the new.

Even though I introduced this bug in the first place, I'd like
to avoid spending additional hours on testing.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] failed stack_alloc tests?
parts:
On Jan 1, 2014 5:46 PM, "Bob Carpenter" <ca...@alias-i.com <mailto:ca...@alias-i.com>> wrote:

    Everything definitely passes on my machine.

    Could we still be running 32-bit mode on Windows?
No, it's 64 bit. I verified by running the executable, checking in task manager for a "*32" at the end.

Or is Windows int sizes (different than *nix) messing
    things up?  I created the test boundaries empirically
    on my machine in clang++ knowing the test fixed things and just
    looking for where the old behavior differs from the new.
Yes. long in Windows isn't long enough and we have integer overflow.

Even though I introduced this bug in the first place, I'd like
    to avoid spending additional hours on testing.
I was able to fix it by replacing long with size_t in the tests and the bytes_allocated() function. I'll update the pull request.

- Bob
